children: High-end computer infrastructure builder and AI cloud services company CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV, Financials) is returning to the public markets.
The company is seeking to sell $3 billion of convertible senior notes due 2033. The buyers will also have an option for an additional $500 million, bringing the offering to $3.5 billion.
The funding arrives as CoreWeave is investing heavily to keep up with the demand for AI computing.

CoreWeave said it plans to use some of the cash to support capped-call transactions to reduce potential dilution from the convertible notes. The balance will be used for general company purposes. The bigger number is on the balance sheet.
In its most recent quarterly filing, CoreWeave disclosed long-term debt of $27.56 billion and short-term debt of $7.51 billion. That is more than $35 billion, before the proposed notes.

It's growing swiftly, having recently deployed a multi-rack Nvidia Vera Rubin cluster into production and securing long-term infrastructure deals as clients battle for AI capacity. But that growth takes huge amounts of finance.

The next key information for investors will be when CoreWeave prices the notes. What investors are demanding to provide it another multibillion-dollar round of financing for its AI expansion will be told by the interest rate and conversion terms.

title: CoreWeave seeks up to $3.5 billion more as debt load tops $35 billion
